comment: Living-requirements store. Mutated only through scripts/loop.mjs, which validates against scripts/loop/lib/validate.mjs and appends every material mutation to state/decisions.jsonl. Statuses: proposed, accepted, active, verified, rejected, deferred, retired. Priorities are 1 (highest) to 5. Costs are S/M/L. See docs/EVOLUTION.md for the mutation rules.

requirements.title: Smallest playable loop: Smoke on the North Wind
requirements.observation: The world is explorable and visually mature (audit pass 99 universal averages 3.8-4.3), but there is nothing to do: three NPCs each speak one static line, there are no objectives, no arrival events, no consequences, and no saved state. The game is a map-scale test bed (README), which violates pillars P4 and P5 and is the single largest player-facing gap.
requirements.playerExperience: A first-time player who enters the world is given a purpose by a family member, travels to it, arrives at a place that responds, discovers something, returns, and sees the family's situation change because of what they did.
requirements.expectedBenefit: Converts the project from a diorama into a game; every later Episode 1 requirement builds on this spine.
requirements.source: Play inspection of the runnable build 2026-08-28: NPCs in src/main.js are static capsules with one line; there is no objective, waypoint, or mission state anywhere in src/.
acceptance: A player who enters the world sees a current objective in the HUD until the loop is complete
Talking to Harlan Calder starts the loop and changes what the HUD asks for
Reaching the objective's location transitions the loop to a new stage with a new prompt
An examine interaction at the burn site yields a discovery recorded in game state
Reporting back to Nell Calder ends the loop, and Nell's and Harlan's dialogue afterward reflects the outcome
The full loop is traversable with a normal controller path: walk/ride, E to interact, no debug-only actions required in the acceptance route
A scripted browser probe drives all transitions headlessly and exits 0
verification: independent fresh-context critic on the runnable build

history.note: proposed by first autonomous inspection; accepted as the first campaign after ranking against travel-without-purpose and save/load gaps

20260829-R1: R1 verified accepted by critic-fork-1. Smallest loop 'Smoke on the North Wind' playable end to end with real controls; 2 reviewer findings fixed post-verification, 2 deferred to R2 (save seam hardening).

requirements.title: Mission progress survives save/load and failure recovery
requirements.observation: There is no save anywhere in src/. localStorage is used only for the dev speed tuning key. Pillar P8 makes save/load a production requirement; today a reload erases every interaction.
requirements.playerExperience: A player who closes the tab mid-loop, or whose renderer dies, resumes where the story left off instead of starting over.
requirements.expectedBenefit: Makes the loop from R1 durable and unlocks every later episode requirement, which all assume a save schema.
requirements.source: grep for localStorage/save across src/ — only src/debug.js touches it.
acceptance: Loop progress is autosaved on every stage transition
A reload restores the mission in the same stage with the same flags
A corrupt or version-mismatched save fails safe: the game boots fresh, the failure is logged, the player is not stuck
A deterministic round-trip test fails if a stage or flag is lost
verification: fault injection (corrupt the save, confirm recovery)

history.note: split out of R1 so the loop itself lands first and save/load is verified independently

20260829-R2: R2 verified accepted by critic-fork-2. Autosave on every stage transition + unload; reload restores stage, flags and pose; torn, foreign-version and impossible-stage saves all fail safe in browser and dry checks.

requirements.title: Travel with purpose: destinations are announced, legible, and findable
requirements.observation: The 4000x5000 m map is rideable and richly dressed, but nothing tells a player where to go or why; the minimap shows geography only. First-time players see an open world with no invitation.
requirements.playerExperience: When an objective names a place, the player can find it: the HUD names the destination, the minimap or world marks it, and legibility holds at 14.5 m/s gallop.
requirements.expectedBenefit: Turns empty travel into meaningful travel (P5); multiplies the value of every future mission.
acceptance: Every active objective resolves to a named, reachable place
A player unfamiliar with the map can reach the objective using only in-game affordances, verified by a traversal probe
No objective requires consulting the README or the repo
verification: targeted visual review of marker legibility
requirements.source: Play inspection 2026-08-28: hud-hint and hud-place are the only guidance surfaces.

history.note: proposed; may be satisfied by R1's initial HUD + marker affordance, in which case retire it with evidence

requirements.title: Dialogue is a conversation, not a poster
requirements.observation: Each NPC stringifies one `line`; pressing E during dialogue closes it. No continuation, no branching, no state-aware content (docs/BACKLOG.md Episode-1 systems: relationship notes, reputation, clues, decisions).
requirements.playerExperience: Talking to a character advances meaning: lines continue, choices appear where the story needs them, and post-mission dialogue reflects what happened.
requirements.expectedBenefit: Prerequisite for P2 (family-centered drama) and for Episode 1's dialogue-set reuse plan.
acceptance: Multi-line dialogue advances with the existing E/click affordance and exits on its last line
At least one dialogue is conditional on world state (mission stage or a discovered flag)
No dialogue reverts to stale text after a consequence changes it
verification: browser play probe of a two-line and a conditional dialogue

requirements.title: Arrival at a place is an event
requirements.observation: placeLabel() changes a HUD string; nothing else responds to arrival. Pillar P1 says arriving should feel like an event; currently only proximity to an NPC does anything.
requirements.playerExperience: Reaching a POI for the first time gives the player a moment: the place is named, and the world acknowledges arrival (beat, prompt, or hook for discovery).
acceptance: First arrival at each of the 16 POIs produces a visible, non-blocking acknowledgement
Repeat visits do not repeat the fanfare
Does not regress the capture tooling (`?dev` hooks unaffected)
verification: browser play probe on two POIs

history.note: proposed; overlaps R1's stage-arrival transitions — fold in or retire after R1 lands

requirements.title: The sky is weather, not a gradient
requirements.observation: The visible sky (src/environment.js createSky) is a static three-stop gradient sphere whose mid/bottom stops are cream and beige, with a flat hard-edged white sun disc and no clouds in any of 32 fresh captures at 16 POIs x 2 sun angles. Scene fog (0x9bb4c8) does not match the sky's own horizon stop (0xf0e2c4), so every distant ridge hazes into a color the air above it does not contain. The sky occupies 25-45% of every player frame and is the largest single 'procedural prototype' tell.
requirements.playerExperience: The player enters a world with weather and air: a soft-lit horizon that distant ridges fade into, drifting clouds that give time of day, and a sun that feels like the source of the warm light — instead of an empty cream dome with a white disc. In every frame, at every destination, during all travel.
requirements.expectedBenefit: Directly serves P1 (distance becomes something to look at and travel toward) and P6 (visual cohesion — nothing screams 'algorithm' louder than an empty gradient sky). Retunes the fog/sky relationship that also drives the salmon-pink golden-hour wash finding.
acceptance: At both captured sun angles (midday, golden), fresh captures show: distant terrain fading into a haze whose hue matches the sky at the horizon, and no flat hard-edged sun disc — a layered sun (bright core plus soft halo) whose tint/intensity varies with elevation
Clouds are visible at representative viewpoints (thin cirrus plus a few cumulus masses), drift slowly during extended play without popping, and fade toward/below the horizon
Cloud coverage is tunable for A/B (dev affordance), defaulting to the accepted look

No regression: terrain readability, golden-hour shadow strength, and horizon banding judged on before/after re-captures of badlands-golden, ranch-golden, overlook-golden and timberCamp-golden (eye); frame time within noise on the same views
verification: focused before/after capture comparison on the 4 regression views plus both sun angles
independent fresh visual critic with the exact perceptual question
frame-time spot check versus the captured before set
requirements.source: Fresh-critic visual discover pass (E8) on audit/visual-campaign-V0 and -V0-eye, 2026-08-29. First campaign of the new autonomous loop: a fresh independent visual critic inspected current pixels and picked this over bare settlement walls, roads-as-paint-stripes, golden pink wash, and placeholder destination props.

history.note: created from the fresh-critic visual discover pass; first production campaign under the new autonomous loop per the operator's explicit first-campaign requirement (R4 deferred, see decisions log)

20260829-R6: First production campaign of the new autonomous loop: fresh-critic visual discover pass picked the empty/cream sky as the highest-value visible gap; implemented elevation-driven palettes, fog-from-horizon, layered HDR sun, drifting FBM clouds; independently verified ACCEPT by critic-visual-1 on before/after captures. Backlog noted: sun rim feather, cloud tiling break, horizon speck aliasing.

requirements.title: Sky finish: sun rim feather, cloud tiling break, horizon speck aliasing
requirements.observation: Critic-visual-1 accepted R6 with three recorded weaknesses: the sun core rim is still a crisp pasted-plate edge against the halo (visible at eye height in timberCamp/burn golden frames); the two-layer FBM cloud field reads as stamped repeated fans in the upper sky (ranch/northernPines/westernRange); the smallest near-horizon cloud specks alias into confetti on flat-horizon views; two single-frame FPS dips (cemetery-midday 49, ranch-golden 51) sit within capture noise but correlate with sky-heavy frames.
requirements.playerExperience: The sky stays believable at every vantage and time of day: the sun is a source of light rather than a pasted plate, cloud shapes never repeat recognisably, and no aliasing shimmers at the horizon during travel.
requirements.expectedBenefit: Removes the three strongest remaining procedural tells in the sky (backlog from the first accepted visual campaign); protects the frame budget on sky-heavy views.
acceptance: The sun core blends into its halo with no hard rim at any captured vantage, midday and golden
No visible fan/stamp repetition in the cloud field across the regression views of R6
No pixel-jagged cloud specks at the horizon in the flat-horizon views (elPaso/westernRange midday, lakeMercy golden)
No systematic FPS drop versus the R6 V1 sweep on the same 32-frame sets
verification: focused before/after captures on the R6 regression views
requirements.source: Independent verification of R6 (critic-visual-1) backlog items; E9 capture sets are the before evidence.
